sections.title: MID-MO VALLEY/MID-MS VALLEY/CNTRL TO NRN PLAINS
sections.text: SOUTHWEST FLOW WILL BE IN PLACE ACROSS THE CNTRL AND NRN PLAINS TODAY AS AN UPPER-LEVEL TROUGH APPROACHES THE REGION FROM THE SOUTHWEST. A THUNDERSTORM COMPLEX POSSIBLY CONTAINING A WIND DAMAGE AND HAIL THREAT IS FORECAST TO DEVELOP EARLY THIS MORNING IN NW MO AND MOVE SEWD ACROSS THE REMAINDER OF MO AFTER DAYBREAK. AS DESTABILIZATION TAKES PLACE TODAY IN THE OZARKS AND MID-MS VALLEY...THE CONVECTIVE CLUSTER MAY REGENERATE OR REMAIN STRONG MOVING SEWD INTO THE NE AR AND WRN TN. FURTHER TO THE NORTHWEST ACROSS THE CNTRL AND NRN PLAINS...A LARGE AREA OF MODERATE INSTABILITY SHOULD DEVELOP BY EARLY AFTERNOON. SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE FORECAST TO INITIATE ON THE WRN EDGE OF MODERATE INSTABILITY IN NE CO...WRN NEB AND SRN SD AS LARGE-SCALE ASCENT MOVES OUT INTO THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS AHEAD OF THE UPPER-LEVEL TROUGH. THE MODERATE INSTABILITY AND STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR EVIDENT ON FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR SUPERCELLS ESPECIALLY WITH THE STORMS THAT REMAIN DISCRETE. HOWEVER...A WIND DAMAGE THREAT SHOULD ALSO EXIST WITH THE MORE PERSISTENT LINE-SEGMENTS. DUE TO SUBSTANTIAL DIRECTIONAL SHEAR IN THE BOUNDARY LAYER...THE MORE INTENSE DISCRETE STORMS MAY ALSO HAVE A TORNADO

sections.title: ERN CAROLINAS/SRN GA
sections.text: MODERATE INSTABILITY IS AGAIN FORECAST TO DEVELOP IN THE COASTAL PLAINS OF THE CAROLINAS AND SRN GA THIS AFTERNOON. STORMS SHOULD INITIATE ALONG THE NWRN EDGE OF MODERATE INSTABILITY EARLY THIS AFTERNOON WHERE LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES ARE FORECAST TO BE QUITE STEEP. THIS MAY RESULT IN A MARGINAL WIND DAMAGE THREAT WITH THE STRONGER CELLS CONCENTRATED AROUND PEAK HEATING. ..BROYLES/ROGERS.. 06/13/2011

sections.title: NRN/CNTRL PLAINS INTO MID MO VALLEY
sections.text: POTENT SHORT WAVE TROUGH OVER THE DAKOTAS WILL LIFT NEWD INTO MANITOBA IN ADVANCE OF NEXT UPSTREAM SYSTEM WHICH WILL TRANSLATE FROM THE COLUMBIA PLATEAU AND GREAT BASIN INTO THE NRN AND CNTRL HIGH PLAINS BY TUE MORNING. IN THE LOW-LEVELS...OCCLUDED FRONT ATTENDANT TO THE DAKOTAS SHORT WAVE TROUGH WILL MAKE ONLY SLOW EWD PROGRESS INTO THE ERN DAKOTAS TODAY. FARTHER S...AN EWD/NEWD ELONGATION OF WRN KS SURFACE LOW IS FORECAST WITH AN INFLECTION IN THE LOW-LEVEL MASS FIELD DEVELOPING INTO NERN KS BY LATE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. BETWEEN THE DAKOTAS OCCLUDED FRONT/INVERTED TROUGH AND THE KS SURFACE LOW...ELY LOW-LEVEL FLOW WILL MAINTAIN A CORRIDOR OF 60S F DEWPOINTS ACROSS NEB/NRN KS...EXTENDING WWD INTO NERN CO AND THE NEB PNHDL. THIS MOISTURE WILL COINCIDE WITH A PLUME OF STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES...YIELDING AFTERNOON MLCAPE OF 1500-3000 J/KG. THE COMBINATION OF GRADUALLY LOWERING MIDLEVEL HEIGHTS AND LOW-LEVEL UPSLOPE FLOW REGIME SHOULD PROMOTE THE DEVELOPMENT OF SCATTERED TSTMS THIS AFTERNOON FROM ERN WY/NERN CO INTO WRN NEB. HERE...THE PRESENCE OF THE ELY SURFACE WINDS AND WLY 40-50 KT FLOW IN THE MIDLEVELS /REF. 12Z DEN AND LBF SOUNDINGS/ WILL RESULT IN MORE THAN SUFFICIENT VERT

sections.title: LOWER MO VALLEY INTO LOWER MS VALLEY
sections.text: MULTIPLE CLUSTERS OF ELEVATED TSTMS ARE DEVELOPING ALONG THE ERN EDGE OF THE CNTRL/SRN PLAINS CAP WITHIN THE EXIT REGION OF A NOCTURNALLY VEERING 50 KT LLJ. VISIBLE SATELLITE SUGGESTS THAT RATHER STRONG DIABATIC HEATING SHOULD COMMENCE TODAY DOWNSTREAM FROM THIS ACTIVITY FROM SRN MO INTO THE LOWER MS VALLEY. WHEN COUPLED WITH THE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER AND ERN EDGE OF EML /SEE 12Z SGF SOUNDING/...EXPECT AFTERNOON AIR MASS TO BECOME MODERATELY TO STRONGLY UNSTABLE WITH MLCAPE OF 2000-3000+ J/KG. GIVEN THE 35-45 KT NWLY MIDLEVEL WIND FIELD...THE POTENTIAL WILL EXIST FOR ONE OR MULTIPLE FORWARD-PROPAGATING CONVECTIVE SYSTEMS CAPABLE OF SWATHS OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL. REGENERATIVE UPSTREAM STORM DEVELOPMENT WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE TODAY ALONG THE ERN EDGE OF THE CAP WITH ACTIVITY FOCUSED ALONG OR ON THE IMMEDIATE COOL SIDE OF CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WHICH SHOULD BECOME BETTER-DEFINED WITH TIME ACROSS WRN MO. PRONOUNCED VEERING WINDS WITH HEIGHT COUPLED WITH THE INFLUX OF A MODERATE TO STRONGLY UNSTABLE AIR MASS FROM THE W WILL PROMOTE ORGANIZED STORM MODES INCLUDING SUPERCELLS AND BOWING STRUCTURES WITH A RISK OF LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS AND PERHAPS TORNADOES. ..MEAD/COHEN.. 06/13

sections.title: LOWER MS VALLEY THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: INITIALLY ELEVATED STORMS OVER SE MO/NE AR WILL EVOLVE INTO CLUSTERS OF SURFACE-BASED STORMS BY EARLY AFTERNOON IN NE AR/WRN TN/NW MS AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZES ALONG AND S OF THE STALLED SURFACE FRONT. BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS OF 68-72 F AND TEMPERATURES WARMING WELL INTO THE 90S WILL SUPPORT MODERATE INSTABILITY SWD ACROSS MS THIS AFTERNOON...AS WELL AS STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES. GIVEN THE 25-30 KT NNWLY STEERING FLOW IN THE MIDLEVELS...EXPECT A CONSOLIDATING COLD POOL AND ASSOCIATED STORMS TO MOVE SWD/SSEWD ACROSS MS THROUGH THE AFTERNOON WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR A CORRIDOR OF DAMAGING OUTFLOW WINDS. THIS CONVECTION MAY PERSIST ALL THE WAY TO THE I-10 CORRIDOR WITH A GRADUALLY DIMINISHING RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS BY LATER THIS EVENING.

sections.title: SE NEB/NE KS/NW MO THIS EVENING
sections.text: STRONG SURFACE-BASED INSTABILITY /MLCAPE 3000-4000 J PER KG/ WILL BE PRESENT ALONG THE SLOW-MOVING WARM FRONT FROM WRN MO NWWD TO NEAR THE KS/NEB BORDER. THIS AREA WILL BE NEAR THE NE EDGE OF THE WARMEST EML...AND THE CAP SHOULD BE WEAKENED BY SURFACE HEATING AND LOW-LEVEL ASCENT ALONG THE FRONT. IF STORMS DEVELOP LATE THIS AFTERNOON...THERE WILL BE THE POTENTIAL FOR SUPERCELLS WITH VERY LARGE HAIL AND TORNADOES...GIVEN THE STRONG INSTABILITY... EFFECTIVE SRH AOA 200 M2/S2...AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR AOA 40-50 KT. ANY STORMS THAT FORM WILL THEN PROGRESS SEWD ALONG THE WARM FRONT INTO WRN/CENTRAL MO THIS EVENING INTO EARLY TONIGHT. OVERNIGHT...THERE WILL AGAIN BE THE POTENTIAL FOR ELEVATED STORMS FROM SRN IA INTO N/NE MO IN THE ZONE OF ENHANCED LOW-LEVEL WAA ON THE NOSE OF THE SWLY LLJ. LARGE HAIL WILL BE THE MAIN THREAT WITH THIS ACTIVITY.

sections.title: CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: A LOW-LEVEL UPSLOPE FLOW REGIME WILL BECOME ESTABLISHED LATER THIS AFTERNOON AS SURFACE PRESSURES FALL IN THE LEE OF THE CENTRAL ROCKIES...IN ADVANCE OF A SHORTWAVE TROUGH MOVING EWD FROM NV/UT. BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE 50S TO NEAR 60 F WILL BE DRAWN WWD LATER THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING...WHERE SURFACE HEATING OVER THE E SLOPES OF THE HIGH TERRAIN COULD INITIATE STORMS. ANY STORMS THAT FORM COULD DEVELOP SUPERCELL STRUCTURES GIVEN THE PRESENCE OF MODERATE MOISTURE/INSTABILITY AND SUFFICIENT DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE MAIN SEVERE THREATS...THOUGH AN ISOLATED TORNADO OR TWO WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE. OVERNIGHT...STORMS COULD EVOLVE INTO A CLUSTER OR TWO THAT WILL PROGRESS EWD OVER THE HIGH PLAINS...IN ADVANCE OF THE APPROACHING MIDLEVEL TROUGH FROM THE W. ..THOMPSON/SMITH.. 06/13/2011

sections.title: LOWER MS VALLEY
sections.text: SEVERE MCS WITH MATURE COLD POOL CONTINUES TO PROPAGATE SWD VICINITY AND JUST E OF MS RIVER. WITH MLCAPES RANGING UPWARDS TO 2500 J/KG AND DCAPES IN EXCESS OF 1200 J/KC...DAMAGING WINDS STILL EXPECTED TO ACCOMPANY THE COMPLEX AS IT TRACKS SWD AT 35KT...POSSIBLY REACHING GULF THIS EVENING PRIOR TO DISSIPATING.

sections.title: SE NEB/NE KS/NW MO
sections.text: PER MODELS AND ACARS SOUNDINGS THE WARM SECTOR REMAINS STRONGLY CAPPED ACROSS KS INTO WRN MO. WITH MUCAPES NOW RANGING UPWARDS TO 4000 J/KG AND VERY STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES IN PLACE COUPLED WITH BRN SHEAR OF 50-60KT...A VERY FAVORABLE CONDITIONAL ENVIRONMENT IS IN PLACE FOR SUPERCELLS INCLUDING A VERY LARGE HAIL THREAT. MODELS PROVIDING MIXED AND INCONCLUSIVE SOLUTIONS AS TO IF/WHEN AND EXACTLY WHERE INITIATION COULD OCCUR. THUS WILL CONTINUE THE POTENTIAL FOR SIGNIFICANT HAIL ALTHOUGH THE OVERALL PROBABILITIES CONTINUE TO REFLECT THE UNCERTAINTY CONCERNING INITIATION. LITTLE CHANGE IN OTHER AREAS INCLUDING THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS AHEAD OF THE APPROACHING S/WV TROUGH. ..HALES.. 06/13/2011 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1130 AM CDT MON JUN 13 2011/

sections.title: CNTRL HIGH PLAINS/NRN PLAINS
sections.text: AN MCS WILL CONTINUE TO ORGANIZE ON THE WRN EDGE OF MODERATE INSTABILITY ACROSS WRN NEB AND NE CO THIS EVENING. ACCORDING TO MESOANALYSIS...THE ENVIRONMENT ACROSS THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS IS CHARACTERIZED BY STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR...MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES EXCEEDING 8.0 C/KM WITH 1500 TO 2500 J/KG OF MLCAPE. THIS SHOULD CONTINUE TO BE SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT AND FAVORABLE FOR LARGE HAIL WITH THE MORE INTENSE UPDRAFTS. THE LARGE HAIL THREAT SHOULD BE ENHANCED OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS IN FAR NE CO AND WCNTRL NEB WHERE A 30 PERCENT HAIL PROBABILITY HAS BEEN MAINTAINED. TORNADOES WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE WITH THE MORE INTENSE SUPERCELLS. SHORT-TERM MODEL FORECASTS AND RADAR TRENDS SUGGEST THE STORMS COULD ORGANIZE INTO A LINE...MOVING EWD ACROSS CNTRL NEB THIS EVENING WHERE THE WIND DAMAGE THREAT MAY INCREASE SOMEWHAT. FURTHER TO THE NORTH ACROSS THE ERN DAKOTAS...A NARROW AXIS OF MODERATE INSTABILITY EXISTS WHERE SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE DEVELOPING. MESOANALYSIS SUGGEST THE GREATEST INSTABILITY AND LOW-LEVEL SHEAR IS LOCATED ACROSS NE ND WHERE AN ISOLATED TORNADO THREAT MAY EXIST FOR ANOTHER HOUR OR TWO...REF MCD 1212.

sections.title: MID-MO VALLEY/CNTRL PLAINS/SRN IA/NRN-CNTRL MO
sections.text: THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT HAS REMAINED RATHER ISOLATED ACROSS THE CNTRL PLAINS MAINLY DUE TO A CAPPING INVERSION EVIDENT ON THE 00Z SOUNDINGS FROM TOPEKA KS AND SPRINGFIELD MO. THE CAPPED AIRMASS IS STRONGLY UNSTABLE WITH MESOANALYSIS SHOWING MLCAPE VALUES FROM NEAR 4000 J/KG IN NRN KS TO ABOUT 3000 J/KG ACROSS WRN MO. IN ADDITION...STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR IS PRESENT ACROSS THE REGION DUE TO SUBSTANTIAL DIRECTIONAL SHEAR IN THE LOW TO MID-LEVELS. THIS ENVIRONMENT WILL EASILY SUPPORT SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT AS THE CAP WEAKENS THIS EVENING ESPECIALLY IF A CLUSTER OF SFC-BASED STORMS CAN INITIATE. THE HRRR MODEL SUGGESTS A CLUSTER OF SUPERCELLS WILL ORGANIZE AND MOVE NEWD ACROSS NE KS AND WRN MO THIS EVENING. IF THIS SCENARIO PANS OUT...THE ENVIRONMENT SHOULD SUPPORT A LARGE HAIL THREAT WITH HAIL OVER 2 INCHES IN DIAMETER POSSIBLE. A TORNADO THREAT SHOULD ALSO EXIST WITH THE MORE DOMINANT SUPERCELLS.

sections.title: LOWER MS VALLEY
sections.text: A CLUSTER OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS CONTINUES TO MOVES SWD ACROSS SRN MS WHERE A POCKET OF MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY IS ANALYZED. THE INSTABILITY ALONG WITH STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE LOWER TO MID 70S F SHOULD BE FAVORABLE FOR DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AS THE STORMS APPROACH THE IMMEDIATE COAST OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. ..BROYLES.. 06/14/2011
